The shop was dark except for the single gas-jet above the counter, and Verloc stood beside it with his hat pulled low, listening. A cart passed in the street; its wheels rumbled and faded. He did not like the stranger’s manner, and he liked still less the thing the stranger had asked him to do. “It is a small matter,” the man had said, smiling thinly. “A small matter, for a man of your experience.” Verloc had said nothing. Now, alone, he went to the back room and sat heavily in a chair, rubbing his heavy-lidded eyes. His wife would be waiting upstairs, and he had no idea how he would explain the look on his face.
